title: Continuous Kähler differentials for an adic algebra
statement: Let $R$ and $B$ be commutative rings, $B$ an $R$-algebra, and $J\subseteq B$ an ideal. For $n\geq 0$ put $E_n=\Omega_{(B/J^{n+1})/R}$, using Kähler differentials and their universal derivations [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], with the $B$-module structure through the quotient map. The quotient map $B/J^{n+2}\to B/J^{n+1}$ induces a $B$-linear map $t_n:E_{n+1}\to E_n$ sending $\mathrm d(b\bmod J^{n+2})$ to $\mathrm d(b\bmod J^{n+1})$. Define $\widehat\Omega_{B/R,J}=\{(z_n)\in\prod_{n\geq0}E_n:t_n(z_{n+1})=z_n\text{ for all }n\geq0\}$, with componentwise addition and $B$-scalar action. Its canonical $R$-derivation is $\widehat{\mathrm d}_{R,J}:B\to\widehat\Omega_{B/R,J}$, $b\mapsto(\mathrm d(b\bmod J^{n+1}))_{n\geq0}$. This is the inverse limit over the positive adic quotients.
